headword: {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}

definitions.explanation: A high-speed train, especially Japan's Shinkansen. The term literally means "bullet train" and was the original nickname for the Shinkansen project before it launched in 1964.

examples.japanese: {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: To go from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.

examples.japanese: {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{時速|じそく}→時速：00128_jisoku⟧300⟦キロ→キロ：01350_kiro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: The bullet train runs at 300 kilometers per hour.

examples.japanese: 1964⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦オリンピック→オリンピック：09899_orinpikku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧、{世界初|せかいはつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開通|かいつう}→開通：04122_kaitsuu⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The world's first bullet train began service in time for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

notes:
Literally "bullet train" — ⟦{弾丸|だんがん}→弾丸：12502_dangan⟧ (bullet) + ⟦{列車|れっしゃ}→列車：01670_ressha⟧ (train). This was the original nickname for the Shinkansen high-speed rail project dating from the wartime era. While ⟦{新幹線|しんかんせん}→新幹線：01053_shinkansen⟧ is the standard term in Japan, {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ} is still used colloquially and is the origin of the English term "bullet train."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{移動|いどう}する→移動する：22430_idousuru⟧: to travel by bullet train
- {弾丸列車|だんがんれっしゃ}⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧: bullet train project (historical)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新幹線|しんかんせん}→新幹線：01053_shinkansen⟧: Shinkansen — the official and far more common term for Japan's high-speed rail
- {高速鉄道|こうそくてつどう}: high-speed railway — the formal, technical term
- ⟦{超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}→超特急：22126_choutokkyuu⟧: super express — an older term for the fastest class of train service

ETYMOLOGY:
The "bullet train" concept originated in a 1939 plan to build a high-speed rail line connecting Tokyo to Shimonoseki. The project was shelved during World War II but revived in the postwar era, culminating in the Tokaido Shinkansen's launch on October 1, 1964.
